subject: Literature
title: J.G. Ballard's The Drowned World
description: A quick win: understand J.G. Ballard's The Drowned World.

hook.text: J.G. Ballard imagined climate change flooding London in 1962, decades before the phrase 'global warming' existed.

buildup.text: Solar radiation melts the ice caps, and London becomes a tropical lagoon filled with giant iguanas and drowned buildings.

discovery.text: Instead of fighting the disaster, the protagonist surrenders to it, finding a strange beauty in civilization's end.

twist.text: Ballard was not writing a survival story. He was exploring how the human mind might welcome its own extinction.

climax.text: The Drowned World pioneered climate fiction and asked whether humanity might accept collapse rather than resist it.

punchline.text: He predicted climate catastrophe before science had a name for it.

quiz.question: What is unusual about the protagonist's response to the flood?
options: He organizes a massive engineering project to drain the water
He surrenders to the disaster and finds beauty in civilization's end
He escapes to higher ground and rebuilds a new city
